q-113019.name: Question 5
q-113019.worked_solution:
To multiply a complex number by a purely imaginary number, we use the distributive property and the fact that ${\text{i}}^{2}=-1.$

For the given problem, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}(7+12\,\text{i})\cdot 5\,\text{i} & =7\cdot 5\,\text{i}+12\,\text{i}\cdot 5\,\text{i} \\  & =(7\cdot 5)\,\text{i}+12\cdot 5\cdot {\text{i}}^{2} \\  & =35\,\text{i}+60\cdot (-1) \\  & =35\,\text{i}-60 \\  & =-60+35\,\text{i}.\end{aligned}
$$

q-218538.name: Question 6
q-218538.worked_solution:
To multiply a complex number by a purely imaginary number, we use the distributive property and the fact that ${i}^{2}=-1.$

For the given problem, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}(-4\,\text{i})\cdot (2+3\,\text{i}) & =(-4\,\text{i})\cdot 2+(-4\,\text{i})\cdot 3\,\text{i} \\  & =(-4)\cdot 2\,\text{i}+(-4)\cdot 3\cdot {\text{i}}^{2} \\  & =-8\,\text{i}+(-12)\cdot (-1) \\  & =-8\,\text{i}+12 \\  & =12-8\,\text{i}.\end{aligned}
$$

q-932.name: Question 7
q-932.worked_solution:
Multiplying two complex numbers is similar to multiplying two binomials. We also use the fact that ${\text{i}}^{2}=-1.$

For the given problem, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}(4+\text{i})(1+5\,\text{i}) & =4\cdot 1+4\cdot 5\,\text{i}+\text{i}\cdot 1+\text{i}\cdot 5\,\text{i} \\  & =4+20\,\text{i}+\text{i}+5\,{\text{i}}^{2} \\  & =4+21\,\text{i}+5\cdot (-1) \\  & =4+21\,\text{i}-5 \\  & =-1+21\,\text{i}.\end{aligned}
$$

q-932.html:
Question 7
?

(4+i)(1+5i)=

a
9+21i
b
−1+20i
c
−1−21i
d
−1+21i
e
9−21i
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Multiplying two complex numbers is similar to multiplying two binomials. We also use the fact that i2=−1.

For the given problem, we have (4+i)(1+5i)=4⋅1+4⋅5i+i⋅1+i⋅5i=4+20i+i+5i2=4+21i+5⋅(−1)=4+21i−5=−1+21i.

q-933.name: Question 8
q-933.worked_solution:
Squaring a complex number means to multiply it by itself, i.e.,

$$
(2+7\,\text{i})^{2}=(2+7\,\text{i})(2+7\,\text{i})
$$

Multiplying two complex numbers is similar to multiplying two binomials. We also use the fact that ${\text{i}}^{2}=-1.$

For the given problem, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}(2+7\,\text{i})^{2} & =(2+7\,\text{i})(2+7\,\text{i}) \\  & =2\cdot 2+2\cdot 7\,\text{i}+7\,\text{i}\cdot 2+7\,\text{i}\cdot 7\,\text{i} \\  & =4+14\,\text{i}+14\,\text{i}+49\,{\text{i}}^{2} \\  & =4+28\,\text{i}+49\cdot (-1) \\  & =4+28\,\text{i}-49 \\  & =-45+28\,\text{i}.\end{aligned}
$$

q-933.html:
Question 8
?

(2+7i)2=

a
54+14i
b
54+28i
c
−45+28i
d
54−28i
e
49+28i
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Squaring a complex number means to multiply it by itself, i.e.,

(2+7i)2=(2+7i)(2+7i)

Multiplying two complex numbers is similar to multiplying two binomials. We also use the fact that i2=−1.

For the given problem, we have (2+7i)2=(2+7i)(2+7i)=2⋅2+2⋅7i+7i⋅2+7i⋅7i=4+14i+14i+49i2=4+28i+49⋅(−1)=4+28i−49=−45+28i.
